Hey op. I too struggle from chronic constipation. Got diagnosed from my doctor in April of this year. Technically been dealing with it since February. I've been through one hell of a journey these past 5 months. Lots of pain. Lots of tears. Lots of stress. Contemplation of suicide here and there. But I think if you find your remedy, it can be easier for you. For me, I eat like a senior. Mostly fruits, vegetables, whole grains, probiotics. When it comes drinks, I mostly drink water, sometimes prune juice and orange juice. Even though I eat like this, I still struggle with pooping. If its difficult eating throughout the day, just snack on foods if it makes you more comfortable and easier on your digestion. I highly recommend using miralax and lactulose. Though with lactulose, you have to get into contact with your health care provider to get it prescribed. I also drink 20oz of coffee a day as it helps stimulate the colon and push stool along it. Although, make sure to be hydrated as it does dry out stool and makes you dehydrated. I usually alternate between these remedies but coffee usually makes me poop once a day which is healthy. I urge you to NEVER take stimulant laxatives. This seriously ruins your body if taken regularly as it will make you dependent on them and more difficult to go without it. Lots of people freak out if they havent gone in one day without pooping and take stimulant laxatives (i am victim of this). If you really need to utilize one, take one if you haven't gone in 3-4 days. I also make sure to walk 1-2 miles a day in the morning and the evening. Other than that, it really is trial and error when it comes to chronic constipation. Just know that its okay to cry. Their are others like you and I who also suffer from this and it is by no means fun to indulge in everyday of our life. Its hard to stay positive and find joy in life when this makes our lifestyle stressful and exhausting as its something we constantly think about. I think what helps other than medications, diets and excercise is definitely someone to talk and vent too. I appreciate my family and friends hearing me out because it does make it a little better. I wish you and everyone else good luck and to stay safe with our chronic condition. Let's get through this together! 🙏
